:::caution[**Mug**, **Kettle** and **Cup** below are RETIRED roles — the Pot is not]
The Mug · Kettle · Cup/nursery **role tier** was **retired 2026-08-09** (owner-directed), so
the present-tense definitions below ("the Mug decides which Cups run", "the Mug places a work
item onto a Cup") describe a tier that no longer runs. `cup:spawn` **refuses**, and
`RETIRED_TIER_ROLES = {mug, kettle, cup}` is enforced after alias canonicalisation, so
`queen`/`bee`/`overwatch` are caught too. **su + GOAL mode are the only way to drive the app**;
fan out with `fleet:launch-on-plan`. See
[the Mug · Kettle · Cup tier is retired](/internal/docs/agent-insights/mug-kettle-cup-tier-is-retired).

The entries are **kept as vocabulary**: these words appear throughout the code, the schema and
the older docs, so a reader still needs to know what they mean. The **Pot** itself is NOT
retired — the pot substrate is explicitly kept (D-003).
:::

<table>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>Term</th>
            <th>Definition</th>
            <th>Example</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Harness</strong></td>
            <td>A long-running iteration loop made of named roles invoked with fresh contexts that hand off via a structured state store.</td>
            <td>The role substrate in <code>libs/papercusp/packages/harness/</code>.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Pot</strong></td>
            <td>An operator over a fleet — a root install minted from a <code>kind:&apos;pot&apos;</code> blueprint. Its single judgment layer (the Mug) surveys the blackboard, decides with agency, creates/supervises harnesses, and declares its own next wake. Distinct from a <code>kind:&apos;harness&apos;</code> blueprint, which is a feature pipeline the Pot creates.</td>
            <td>A coding Pot from the <code>coding</code> blueprint, placing work onto Cups and spinning up <code>coding-factory</code> harnesses per feature.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Blueprint</strong></td>
            <td>The recipe that superseded <em>template</em> — a declared spine of roles, models, dispatch/triggers, and recommended plugins. <code>kind:&apos;pot&apos;</code> blueprints mint a Pot operator; <code>kind:&apos;harness&apos;</code> blueprints mint a feature pipeline.</td>
            <td><code>coding</code> (pot), <code>coding-factory</code> (default pipeline harness), <code>coding-solo</code> (single-worker baseline), <code>research</code>.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Cup</strong></td>
            <td>The generic operator-world worker the Mug places ranked work + a brief onto. Carries no pipeline spine and no chunk requirement (decoupled from the pipeline <code>worker</code> guards); the pipeline roles apply only when a Cup explicitly spins up a coding harness.</td>
            <td>The Mug places a work item onto a Cup, which does the task or spins up a <code>coding-factory</code> harness for it.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Mug</strong></td>
            <td>The Pot blueprint&apos;s placement-specialist decider — the operator role tuned toward placement: <code>cup:spawn</code>/<code>drain</code> and work-list shaping. Same judgment layer as the operator, dial turned toward fleet management.</td>
            <td>The Mug decides which Cups run, drains idle ones, and shapes the ranked work list each wake.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Install</strong></td>
            <td>A specific configured harness — its goal, its plugins, its UI, its DB schema. An install is what users actually run.</td>
            <td>A coding Pot spun up from the <code>coding</code> blueprint. (The original Papercup 5-director autonomous-AI-company demo is retired — preserved-not-active in <code>_retired/papercup</code>; migration 192 dropped the org-simulation tables.)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Role</strong></td>
            <td>A named agent invocation — a <em>prompt file</em> + an entry in the orchestrator's decision table. Always with fresh context.</td>
            <td>The shipped pipeline roles are Scoper, Architect, Worker, Validator, Reviewer, Debugger, Documenter, Curator (the coding-factory pipeline runs scoper &rarr; architect &rarr; worker &rarr; validator &rarr; reviewer &rarr; documenter &rarr; curator). Orchestrator is a separate coordinator/decider role, not a pipeline stage — see <code>AGENT_ROLES</code> in <code>packages/agent-mcp/src/role-config.ts</code>. Plus user-defined roles via plugins.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Harness template</strong></td>
            <td>A reusable recipe for spinning up a harness. One template → many concrete harness <em>instances</em>; each instance has its own goal, project dir, state. Templates declare their roles, default models, and the plugins they recommend.</td>
            <td>The shipped coding blueprints: <code>coding</code> (the <code>kind:&apos;pot&apos;</code> Pot operator), <code>coding-factory</code> (the default per-feature pipeline harness), and <code>coding-solo</code> (the single-worker baseline). One user spins up one <em>instance</em> per project. (The retired <code>papercup-org</code> 5-department company is no longer a spinnable template.)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Plugin</strong></td>
            <td>A package that extends one or more harness instances with new capabilities — actions (buttons), routes, lifecycle hooks, DB schemas, custom UI tabs. Plugins are installed once globally and mounted into harness instances at runtime; their behaviour is gated by capability tiers (§10).</td>
            <td><code>@papercupai/cloudflare-pages</code> contributes a "Publish" button; <code>@papercupai/slack-notifier</code> sends a Slack message on <code>mission-done</code>. The retired <code>@papercupai/vscode-server</code> pilot used to contribute a code-server tab; IDE tabs remain plugin-shaped, not core. Multiple plugins compose per instance.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Marketplace package <code>kind</code></strong></td>
            <td>The discriminator that tells the marketplace + Cupboard which install pipeline a published artifact follows. Implemented as a ten-kind storefront (<code>LISTING_KINDS</code> in <code>packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/types.ts</code>): <code>harness</code> (repo→Pot lookup), <code>blueprint</code> (fork), <code>plugin</code>, <code>pack</code>, <code>knowledge-pack</code>, <code>template</code>, <code>app</code>, <code>rubric</code>, <code>plan</code>, and <code>recipe</code>. The last three distribute grading contracts, reusable plan templates, and runnable tool orchestrations; <code>tool-pack</code>/<code>learning-pack</code> remain normalized aliases and <code>snapshot</code> is retired.</td>
            <td>All ten go through the same publish + retraction infrastructure; the consumer action and install handler differ by kind. <code>blueprint</code>, <code>knowledge-pack</code>, <code>rubric</code>, <code>plan</code>, and <code>recipe</code> listings publish pending and surface only after operator approval.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Goal</strong></td>
            <td>The top-level mission. Every task traces back to a goal through a parent chain. Goals can themselves nest.</td>
            <td>"Build a habit-tracker mobile app and ship to TestFlight" or "Run an autonomous marketing agency."</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><strong>Pending event</strong></td>
            <td>An entry in the queue the orchestrator reads on each tick. Sources: cron routines, webhooks, API triggers, completion deltas.</td>
            <td>Routine "weekly-briefing" fires at 9am Monday → inserts <code>&#123;&#123;role: narrator, due: 09:00&#125;&#125;</code>.</td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
